guideTitle: The Best CPU Stands for Large and Heavy PC Towers
breadcrumbLabel: Best CPU Stands for Large Towers
metaTitle: Best CPU Stands for Large PC Towers: Size and Capacity Compared (2026)
metaDescription: We compared CPU stands for full-size towers on length and width range, stated load rating, casters and extras, from a $14 adjustable stand to a 150 lb GreenForest cart.
introParagraphs: A large gaming or workstation tower is longer and heavier than the cases most budget stands are designed for. The two numbers that matter are the stand's length and width range, which must cover your case's footprint, and its load rating.

Only the GreenForest here states a load rating (150 lb). The Liitrton gives the longest adjustable length, up to 22.44 inches, and VIVO sizes a cart specifically for ATX towers. Others are general-purpose stands; check your case size against each.
Our comparison is based on published specifications and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $14 to $95 at the time of writing.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-1.summary: An adjustable-width stand that lifts the PC 1.75 inches off carpet.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-1.description:
This stand lifts the tower 1.75 inches off the floor with adjustable width and casters, for about $16 at the time of writing.

For a large tower, the problem is that the listing gives no width or length range and no load rating, so confirm your case fits before ordering.
cons: No size range or load rating listed
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-1.skipIf: Your tower is long or heavy; the Liitrton or GreenForest list more.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-2.summary: A Hovadova stand with four 360° casters, locking wheels and tool-free setup.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-2.description:
This Hovadova stand adds locking wheels to the usual four 360-degree casters, which helps stop a heavy tower from rolling when bumped, with tool-free setup, for about $17 at the time of writing.

The listing does not give size range or load rating.
specs: Size range and load rating: not stated
cons: No size range or load rating listed
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-2.bestFor: Towers that should stay put once positioned.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-2.skipIf: You need a stated fit for a long case; the Liitrton lists 22.44 inches.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-3.summary: A ZUAVIALA metal cart adjustable from 21.34 to 28.3 inches high.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-3.description:
The ZUAVIALA raises the tower to 21.34–28.3 inches, near desk height, and adds surface space.

It costs about $41 at the time of writing. The listing does not state a load rating or maximum case size, so confirm a large tower fits the shelf.
specs: Load rating and case size: not stated
cons: Case size and load not stated
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-3.bestFor: Keeping a large tower beside the desk at reach height.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-3.skipIf: You want a stated load rating; the GreenForest lists 150 lb.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-4.summary: A full-metal cart with angle-iron reinforcement, steel casters, storage and a 150 lb rating.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-4.description:
The GreenForest is the one stand here built and rated for heavy towers: a full-metal frame with reinforced angle iron and a bottom crossbar, rated for 150 lb, on steel casters that GreenForest says roll over hardwood, tile and thick carpet and lock in place.

It also adds storage for gaming accessories.

It is the most expensive option here at about $95 at the time of writing and larger than a simple stand.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-4.bestFor: Heavy full towers that need a stated rating.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-4.skipIf: Your tower is light; a $15 stand is enough.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-5.badge: Best Budget Stand for Long Cases
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-5.summary: A Liitrton stand adjustable from 16.93 to 22.44 inches long, on 360° casters.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-5.description:
The Liitrton is the budget pick for large cases because it states its range: 16.93 to 22.44 inches long and adjustable in width from about 9 inches, on four 360-degree casters, for about $15 at the time of writing.

The longer platform supports deep full-tower cases that overhang shorter stands.

The listing does not state a load rating.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-5.bestFor: Long full-tower cases on a budget.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-5.skipIf: You need a stated load rating; the GreenForest lists 150 lb.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-6.summary: The ZUAVIALA tower cart with a built-in power outlet.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-6.description:
This ZUAVIALA adds a power outlet to the desk-height cart, for about $46 at the time of writing.

The listing does not state surge protection, load rating or maximum case size.
specs: Load rating and case size: not stated
cons: Surge protection and capacity not stated
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-6.bestFor: Setups that want an outlet at the tower.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-6.skipIf: You do not need the outlet; the plain ZUAVIALA costs less.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-7.badge: Best Low Cart for ATX Towers
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-7.summary: VIVO's low-profile steel cart sized for large ATX cases.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-7.description:
The VIVO large cart is sized for ATX towers, in steel on four casters, from an established brand, for about $30 at the time of writing.

The listing does not give dimensions or a load rating; check them against your case.
specs: Dimensions and load rating: not stated
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-7.bestFor: Full ATX towers under the desk.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-7.skipIf: You need a stated load rating.

best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-8.summary: A YOSE tower stand with almost no listed specifications.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-8.description:
The YOSE is the cheapest stand here at about $14 at the time of writing, but its listing gives almost no specifications: no size range, load rating or caster details.

For a large tower, that makes it hard to recommend over the Liitrton, which costs about the same and states its size range.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-8.bestFor: Buyers who can confirm fit from the product photos.
best-cpu-stands-for-large-pc-towers-8.skipIf: You want stated dimensions; the Liitrton lists them.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Large towers need a longer platform. The Liitrton lists up to 22.44 inches; VIVO sizes a cart for ATX.
Only the GreenForest states one (150 lb). Weigh your tower and confirm with the seller for others.
Locking or steel casters (Hovadova, GreenForest) keep a heavy tower from rolling.
ZUAVIALA and GreenForest carts raise the tower and add storage; low stands hide it under the desk.

faq.q: Will a standard CPU stand hold a large tower?
faq.a: Check both the size range and the load rating. Many listings state neither; the Liitrton states length and the GreenForest a 150 lb rating.

faq.q: How long should the stand be?
faq.a: At least as long as your case's depth. Full towers can exceed 20 inches.
They stop a heavy PC from rolling when you bump the desk or plug in cables.

bottomLine: For a heavy full tower, the GreenForest is the only stand here with a stated rating and is worth paying more for. On a budget, the Liitrton is the practical choice for long cases because it states its length range.

The VIVO large cart suits ATX towers under the desk, the Hovadova adds locking wheels, and the ZUAVIALA carts bring the tower up to desk height. The YOSE lists too little to recommend for large towers.
